doc.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022

title: Studio B equipment at Electric Lady
summary: The Datamix console, Eddie Kramer and staff, and 8, 16 and 2 inch tape.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Can you recall what kind of recording deck, or what did the booth look like when you first worked there?

Oh yes, very good. It was — At the time I was back in Studio B and it had a Datamix console which — I don’t think there were a lot of them. I think Atlantic had one or two, and Eddie Kramer, who was the founding engineer at the studio, he of course most famous for his work with Jimi Hendrix, and did so many of his recordings. And it was Jimi’s studio. So Eddie would stipulate what the equipment would be and he worked with a great technical staff, a guy named Shimon Ron who was a big help in putting that place together and so forth. And there were other guys around, a wonderful, wonderful engineer, a guy named Dave Palmer who worked with Eddie, he was his first assistant. So there were a lot of people there, and it was outfitted very well. We had — they were still doing 8 track recording, of course 4 track in stereo and mono, but the track count at that point was really a — 16 was just in at that point; 24 track recording hadn’t occurred yet. So you had an MM1000 — basically it was a video desk, an Ampex video desk that they converted to be able to record analog audio. And there would be a 4 track recorder and stereo recorders, and that was the room, aside from the microphones.
And two inch tape? Was that —
Yeah, two inch tape, yeah. The 8 track of course was one inch tape but the 16 track was two inch tape. It sounded great. It was a chunky sound.
I can remember the first time I saw that kind of thing it was like whoa, look at all this stuff.

Yeah I know. Well it hit me like that too. I loved it. It was just, I don’t know, it seemed very real to me. It seemed, it was a way to do something substantial. The quality was high. And I saw an opportunity to have fun and create valuable product with someone else, with musicians. And I loved it. It was great.
